description:
Since arithmetic operators became Kernel calls, no program lowers + - * / rem as a binary op. direct_operator_name (src/compiler2/jobs/body.rs) routes Add, Sub, Mul, Div and Rem to Kernel functions in bodies; fz-rs7.4 did the same for guards (PatternGuardBinOp lost Add..Rem); lowered_binop_ty (jobs/semantic.rs) panics if one is lowered as a binary op. The code that lowers and runs them is reachable only from tests that construct the nodes by hand (for example fz_ir_test).

Candidates, to be confirmed by renaming each with a leading underscore and letting cargo check list dependents:
- IrBinOp::Add, Sub, Mul, Div, Mod and the Add..Rem arms of lower_binop (jobs/native.rs)
- lower_arith_binop, try_typed_binop_fast_path, emit_float_rem (native_codegen/prim.rs); the doc comment above lower_neg in prim.rs describes try_typed_binop_fast_path and goes with it
- as_known_numeric_f64 (native_codegen/value.rs) if nothing else reads it
- the interpreter's int_arith arms
- the tests that only construct those nodes

Comparison operators stay: guards still lower Eq, Neq, Lt, Le, Gt, Ge through lower_guard_binop.

Before deleting, prove unreachability with telemetry or a census rather than by reading: the full fixture matrix and guard matrix run with the arithmetic arms replaced by a loud panic and stay green.

Done when grep finds no arithmetic IrBinOp variant and no function that existed only to lower one.

Acceptance: full gate green; no pin rises.
title: The arithmetic binary-op lowering that no program reaches is deleted
